name: BTS5045-1EJA
title: Single-channel 45 mΩ smart high-side power switch with current sense, PROFET+ 12V
summary: The BTS5045-1EJA is a one-channel high-side switch for 12 V automotive loads: an N-channel vertical power MOSFET driven by an on-chip charge pump, 45 mΩ typical at 25 °C, in a PG-DSO-8-43 EP package whose exposed pad is the supply. It suits lamps up to one P27W/P21W, LEDs, and resistive, inductive or capacitive loads with high inrush. Protection covers voltage-dependent current limiting, absolute and dynamic overtemperature shutdown with automatic restart, an active clamp for inductive turn-off, and, with external parts, overvoltage, reverse battery and loss of ground. A diagnostic pin IS, gated by DEN, returns a current proportional to load current (kILIS about 1460) or a fixed fault current for short circuit, overtemperature and open load.

pins.name: GND
pins.function: Device ground for the logic; returned to module ground through a resistor or diode network (ZGND) in the protection schemes.

pins.name: IN
pins.function: Turns the output channel on when high, off when low.

pins.name: DEN
pins.function: Diagnostic enable: high connects the sense and fault signal to IS; low leaves IS high impedance.

pins.name: IS
pins.function: Sense output: a current proportional to load current, or the fault current IIS(FAULT), while DEN is high.

pins.name: NC
pins.function: No internal connection to the die.

pins.name: OUT
pins.function: Protected high-side output. The three pins are joined inside and must all be joined on the board, with copper sized for the highest current that can flow.

pins.name: VS
pins.function: Exposed cooling tab: the battery supply input and the drain of the power transistor.

circuits.title: Application diagram with a microcontroller and a lamp load
circuits.description: The switch U1 feeds a lamp from the battery through module connectors and cable. A microcontroller drives IN and DEN through 4.7 kΩ resistors and reads the sense current as a voltage across RIS (1.2 kΩ) at its A/D input, through RSENSE and RAD (4.7 kΩ each) with Z1 (7 V) clamping the middle node and CSENSE (100 pF) filtering the A/D input. Device ground returns to module ground through RGND (1 kΩ) in parallel with diode D (BAS21) for reverse-battery protection. CVS (100 nF) and Z2 (36 V) sit across the supply. On the output, RPD (47 kΩ) and COUT0 (4.7 nF) go to ground, and the PNP T1 can switch battery voltage through ROL (1.5 kΩ) onto the output for open-load diagnosis while the channel is off.
notes: The microcontroller side (Vss, CSENSE, Z1, RIS) returns to its own ground VSS; CVS, Z2, RPD, COUT0, RGND, D and the lamp return to module ground GND.

equations.name: Energy dissipated while demagnetising an inductive load
equations.expr: E = VDS(AZ) × (L / RL) × [ ((VS - VDS(AZ)) / RL) × ln(1 - RL × IL / (VS - VDS(AZ))) + IL ]

operation.text: The output transistor is an N-channel vertical DMOS whose gate is driven above the supply by an internal charge pump. RDS(ON) rises with junction temperature (about 27 mΩ at -40 °C to about 80 mΩ at 150 °C, typical) and climbs steeply as VS falls toward 4.5 V. A high level on IN turns the DMOS on with a controlled slope chosen for low EMC emission.

Turn-on delay runs from the IN edge to VOUT reaching 10 % of VS and turn-on time to 90 %; turn-off delay runs to VOUT falling to 90 % and turn-off time to 10 %. Slew rates are measured between 30 % and 70 % of VS.

At turn-off an inductive load drives OUT below ground. An internal clamp ZDS(AZ) between drain and source holds the output at VS - VDS(AZ) so the transistor is not destroyed by avalanche, and the stored energy is dissipated in the device. The single-pulse energy limit EAS (40 mJ at 4 A, TJ(0) = 150 °C, VS = 13.5 V) sets the largest load inductance.

Pulling OUT above VS drives a current IINV from OUT back to VS through the body diode of the power transistor. IN still controls the output, but an IN change from low to high during inverse current takes effect only once the inverse current has stopped. Inverse current reads as open load: open load in OFF with the channel off, open load in ON with the channel on, overtemperature reporting then being blocked. A spurious diagnostic may show at the onset of VINV; after that, and once VINV has gone, the diagnosis is valid. No protection function acts during inverse current.

If module or device ground is lost while the load stays grounded, the device turns off or stays off whatever IN does. A small current IOUT(GND) (0.1 mA typ at VS = 28 V) can still leave OUT. Series resistors between the microcontroller and IN/DEN are recommended so the channel turns off when device ground is lost. ZGND may be a resistor or a diode.

Below VS(UV) (3.5 V typ) the switch is off. It can be switched on once VS exceeds VS(OP); between the two thresholds the undervoltage mechanism governs, VS(UV) being the lowest supply at which the switch stays on. With the switch on the protections work, but the diagnosis is guaranteed only within VNOM (8 V to 18 V).

The internal Zener ZD(AZ) protects the logic section; a resistor in the ground path keeps its current in bounds. Above VS(AZ) (47 V typ) the power transistor turns on and the logic supply is clamped, so the internal ground rises to VS - VS(AZ), and IN and DEN follow it closely through their ESD Zeners, depending on the impedance driving them. A channel that was on stays on, and one that was off may turn on. Between VBAT(SC) and VDS(AZ) the output still follows IN, but in the ON state the parameters are not guaranteed and life is reduced, short-circuit robustness and EAS most of all. A 150 Ω resistor as ZGND performs better than a diode with 1 kΩ.

With the battery reversed the body diode conducts, its current limited by the load, and dissipates power. Ground and logic-pin currents must be kept within the absolute maximum ratings by external resistors: RGND limits the current in the internal Zener, RDEN and RIN the current into the logic and ESD structures, and RSENSE what flows through the sense transistor, which behaves like a diode then. Recommended values are RDEN = RIN = RSENSE = 4.7 kΩ. ZGND is either a 150 Ω resistor or a Schottky diode with 1 kΩ in parallel; where overvoltage is not a concern RGND can be the Schottky and 1 kΩ, optionally with a parallel capacitor for EMC. No protection works under reverse polarity.

On overload (cold lamp inrush, short to ground) the current is first limited to IL(SC), which depends on VDS: typically about 32 A up to VDS = 15 V, falling to about 16 A above 20 V. The limit also changes as the DMOS heats.

The channel has an absolute sensor (shutdown at TJ(SC), 170 °C typ) and a dynamic sensor (trip on a rise ΔTJ(SW), 80 K typ). Either one turns the channel off, and it stays off until the temperature has fallen enough; it then turns back on if IN is still high, repeating the cycle. ΔTSTEP is the warming caused by the overcurrent.

With DEN low, IS is high impedance. With DEN high, IS carries either IL / kILIS or, for a short to ground, current limiting, overtemperature, a too-fast temperature rise, or open load while off, the fault current IIS(FAULT) (15 mA typ). How accurate the sense is varies with load current and temperature. During restart cycling with DEN high, IS stays at IIS(FAULT) and does not toggle.
A pull-down RIS on IS turns the sense current into a voltage. RIS must be above 560 Ω to keep losses in the sense circuit down; 1.2 kΩ is typical.
kILIS may be calibrated in the application at one point (IL3, TJ = 25 °C); the remaining drift with current and temperature is then bounded by ΔkILIS (±5 %, kILIS3 against kILIS2).

With the channel on and DEN high, a load current below IL(OL) (5 mA to 30 mA) is flagged: the sense current then falls below IIS(OL) (8 µA). Above IL(OL) the sense current stays above IIS(OL). Leakage through a broken load, from humidity for example, can keep some current flowing.

An external pull-up ROL from the output to the battery is recommended for off-state open-load detection, sized against the open-load threshold VOL(OFF) and all leakage in the system (IL(OFF) plus external leakage from humidity or corrosion). A switch SOL in series with ROL keeps standby current low. With the channel off and no load, VOUT rises to near VS; when VS - VOUT falls below the threshold, IS switches to IIS(FAULT). An optional RPD pulls OUT to 0 V when it would otherwise float, and also serves short-to-battery detection. Between the falling edge of IN and the rising edge of DEN a delay tsIS(OT_BLANK) is needed before an off-state open-load request, or VOUT is not settled and the result can be wrong.

A short from OUT to VS carries part or all of the load current, so less flows through the DMOS and the sense current drops. With the channel off, the open-load comparator with a resistor RSC_VS from OUT to ground detects the short to battery.
Overload means the current reaching its limit, the dynamic temperature swing reaching ΔTJ(SW), or TJ reaching TJ(SC); IS then gives IIS(FAULT) when DEN is high.

IN and DEN are threshold inputs for 3.3 V and 5 V logic with a Schmitt trigger (250 mV typ hysteresis), so a slow edge cannot leave the output in a linear state, and they accept PWM. The switching point lies between VIN(L) max (0.8 V) and VIN(H) min (2 V) and varies with process and temperature. DEN has the same structure as IN. An unused input is left open or tied to device ground (not module ground) through a resistor.

RthJA of 40 K/W is for a 2s2p FR4 board of 76.4 × 114.3 × 1.5 mm with 70 µm outer and 35 µm inner copper and vias beneath the exposed pad. On a single-layer 1s0p board RthJA falls from about 98 K/W on the footprint alone to about 47 K/W with 600 mm² of copper.
Typical curves are characterised on 3 lots of 3 devices at 8 V, 13.5 V and 18 V across temperature; a single curve is the 13.5 V result where supply voltage has no effect.
